summary: Gajanan Balkrishna Palsule was an Indologist and linguist. He worked as a sub-editor in the Dictionary Department at Deccan College (~1950–1960) and held a post at Savitribai Phule Pune University (~1960–1981).

Working in Iranian and Central Asian studies, Buddhist studies, and linguistics, Galsang Gomboev studied under Józef Szczepan Kowalewski. From 1855 to 1863, he taught Mongolian at Saint Petersburg State University.

Gananath Obeyesekere studied at the University of Peradeniya and University of Washington. Working in religious and Buddhist studies, he taught at Peradeniya (~1958–1971), UC San Diego (~1972–1980), and Princeton University (1980–2000), where he became Emeritus Professor of Anthropology.

Ganesh Prasad studied at the University of Calcutta and University of Allahabad. Active in history and archaeology, he headed a department at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (1905) and held posts at Calcutta (~1914–1918) and Banaras Hindu University (~1918–1923).

Working in Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies, Ganganatha Jha studied at Calcutta, Allahabad, and Sampurnanand Sanskrit University. He worked at Raj Darbhanga, served as Sanskrit professor at Muir Central College (1902–1918), and was vice-chancellor of Allahabad (1923–1932).

Gangzhun is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Qinghai Nationalities University until 1989 and completed a master's degree at Northwest Minzu University (1998–2001) under Alak Dorje Rinpoche.

Ganzorig Davaa-Ochir is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned an M.Phil. in Tibetan Studies at the University of Oslo under Hanna Havnevik and also studied under Lama Byambaa (both attested 2008).
Garab Dorje Rinpoche is a figure in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He pursued traditional studies under Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje and Thinley Norbu Rinpoche.

Garcin de Tassy studied at the Collège de France under Jean-Daniel Kieffer and Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy. A scholar of Indology and linguistics who founded the Société Asiatique, he held an Indian languages chair at INALCO/École des langues orientales (~1828–1878).

Gareth Fisher specializes in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. He earned his Ph.D. in socio-cultural anthropology from the University of Virginia (by 2006) and served as Assistant Professor of Religion and Anthropology at Syracuse University (attested 2011–2016).

Gareth Sparham studied at McGill, the Institute of Buddhist Dialectics, and the University of British Columbia under Ashok Aklujkar. Active in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology, he held posts at UBC (~1989–1999) and taught Tibetan at Michigan (1999–2009).

Gary A. Tubb is an Indologist who studied under Daniel H. H. Ingalls. He held faculty posts at Harvard University (attested 1999), Columbia University (attested 2007), and the University of Chicago (attested 2011).

Working in religious and Buddhist studies, Gary D. DeAngelis studied under Masatoshi Nagatomi, George Rupp, W. J. Johnson, Herbert Mason, and Muhammad Daud Rahbar. He served as Associate Director of the Center for Interdisciplinary Studies at Holy Cross (attested 2017).

Gary Snyder studied at Reed College, Indiana University, and UC Berkeley under Shih-Hsiang Chen, as well as under traditional teachers. Active in religious and Buddhist studies, he served as a professor at UC Davis (1986–2002).

Gary Urton studied at Eastern New Mexico University, the University of New Mexico, and the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign. An anthropology and history scholar, he held faculty posts at Colgate University (1978–2002) and Harvard University (2012–2020).

Gaspare Gorresio was an Indologist who studied at the University of Turin, under Amedeo Peyron, Eugène Burnouf, and Stanislas Julien. He held Turin's chair in Sanskrit (1852) and served as librarian at the Royal Library of Turin (~1852–1891).

Gaston Paris was a linguist who studied under Friedrich Christian Diez and at the École des chartes. He held posts at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1869–1903) and the Collège de France (1872–1903).
Gaston Renondeau was a scholar of Japanology and Buddhist studies who studied at the École Polytechnique (~1899–1901).
Gaton Ngawang Lekpa was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thaye and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo.

Gauri Viswanathan is an Indology and religious studies scholar. She studied at the University of Delhi and Columbia University, taught English at Delhi (~1973–1978), and became Class of 1933 Professor and South Asia Institute director at Columbia (~1989).
